content.title: Braylon Mullins' dad has 6-word reaction to UConn game winner
content.text: The UConn Huskies have had many heroes during their program's March Madness runs, and freshman Braylon Mullins became the latest after his incredible shot to dethrone the No. 1 overall seed Duke Blue Devils in the East Region.With a trip to the Final Four on the line, Duke dominated UConn throughout the game. Despite big man Taris Reed Jr. carrying the team, the other Huskies also shot horribly from long-range, unable to find any three-pointers most of the night.That was until they stormed back to make things interesting in the final stretch of the game. After Silas Demary Jr. made one of his two free throws with just 10 seconds on the clock, Duke needed to inbound the clock and get fouled or run the clock out.However, the Huskies used pressure defense on the full-court inbound, and Mullins forced a turnover, giving the Huskies a chance to tie or take a lead. They did the latter on a heroic shot by Mullins, who connected from near the logo on a three, giving UConn a 73-72 lead with 0.4 left in the game.Duke was unable to come up with a full-court heave and game-winner, getting stunned before the final buzzer by the No. 2 seed UConn.Read more: UConn’s Braylon Mullins Has Strong Reaction to Game-Winning Shot vs DukeWASHINGTON, DC - MARCH 29: Braylon Mullins #24 celebrates with Jayden Ross #23 and Malachi Smith #0 of the UConn Huskies after Mullins shot the game-w... | Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty ImagesThe big hero was Mullins due to his epic shot, which joins other Huskies greats in the history books. While Mullins didn't have his best shooting night, he came up clutch at just the right time, with a half-court three Steph Curry would've been proud of.Speaking of the Golden State Warriors, there may be some misconceptions about Braylon Mullins being related to Warriors legend Chris Mullin, but they have different spellings of their last names.However, Braylon Mullins' dad was also a witness to his son's incredible shot. Active on X (formerly Twitter), Josh Mullins fired off a six-word message reacting to his son and UConn going to the Final Four."INDY.... HOLLA IF YA HEAR ME!!!" Mullins' dad wrote, adding a hashtag for "FINAL4" with the message.This year's Final Four for the NCAA Tournament takes place in Indianapolis, Indiana. UConn will face Illinois next, with the winner advancing to play either Michigan or Arizona for the championship.Fittingly, Braylon Mullins hails from Greenfield, Indiana, played his high school ball for Greenfield-Central High School, and now gets to play again in his home state in front of his family, including his father.Mullins, considered among NBA Draft picks in June, is also known as "Indiana Mr. Basketball," an award he received from The Sporting News as the state's top basketball player, becoming a highly sought-after recruit that Hurley and UConn landed. Previous winners include fellow tournament star, Braden Smith of Purdue, and former NBA great Glenn "Big Dog" Robinson.For Braylon, basketball definitely runs in the family, too. His father, Josh, played for Lincoln Trail College and Indiana University-Purdue University, Indianapolis (IUPUI).The younger Mullins has immediately become one of UConn's March Madness heroes, thanks to his late-game shot, which tipped the lead in favor of UConn with 0.4 on the clock.Read more: UConn’s Dan Hurley Clarifies Luke Murray ‘Goodbye’ Amid March MadnessFor more about college basketball, visit Newsweek Sports.
